docs.title: Claude Code Configuration
docs.text: This guide explains how to configure Claude Code (Anthropic's CLI tool) to use the RIDDL MCP Server for AI-assisted domain modeling.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Claude Code CLI installed (npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code)
  • riddlg installed and on your PATH (see Installation): 
    brew install ossuminc/tap/riddlg

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
The quickest way is the claude mcp command, which registers riddlg mcp as a stdio server:

claude mcp add riddl -- riddlg mcp

To make it available in every project, add --scope user:

claude mcp add --scope user riddl -- riddlg mcp

docs.title: Project-Level Configuration
docs.text:
To share the server with everyone who checks out a project, add a .mcp.json file at the project root:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

Claude Code picks this up automatically when you run it in that directory. No URL and no API key are involved — Claude Code launches riddlg mcp for you.

docs.title: Verify Connection
docs.text:
Start Claude Code and ask it to test the connection:

claude

Then in the session:

"Can you validate this RIDDL: domain Test is { ??? }"

Claude should use the riddl_validate tool and return results. You can also list configured servers with claude mcp list.

docs.title: Validating RIDDL Files
docs.text:
When working in a directory with .riddl files:

"Please validate the file src/domain.riddl"

Claude Code can read the file and use the RIDDL MCP server to validate it.

docs.title: Creating New Models
docs.text:
"Help me create a RIDDL model for a hotel reservation system with bookings, rooms, and guests"

Claude will use map-domain-to-riddl to suggest a structure, then help you refine it.

docs.title: Fixing Validation Errors
docs.text:
"I'm getting validation errors in my RIDDL file. Can you explain them and suggest fixes?"

Claude will use riddl_validate and explain-error to help you resolve issues.

docs.title: Checking Model Quality
docs.text:
"Check if my order management model is complete enough for simulation"

Claude will use check-completeness and check-simulability to analyze your model.

docs.title: Available RIDDL Tools
docs.text:
Tool Use Case riddl_validate Check RIDDL source for errors riddl_outline Summarize a model's definitions validate-partial Check incomplete/in-progress models check-completeness Find missing elements check-simulability Verify simulation readiness map-domain-to-riddl Convert descriptions to RIDDL explain-error Understand validation errors suggest-next Get recommendations for next steps

See MCP Tools for the full catalog of 13.

docs.title: Server Not Connecting
docs.text:
• Run claude mcp list to confirm riddl is registered
  • Verify riddlg mcp starts from a terminal (it waits on stdin; Ctrl+C to exit)
  • If riddlg isn't found, register it by absolute path: claude mcp add riddl -- /opt/homebrew/bin/riddlg mcp

docs.title: Tools Not Available
docs.text:
• Restart Claude Code after configuration changes
  • Check riddlg version runs successfully

docs.title: Tips for Effective Use
docs.text:
1. Be specific: Instead of "validate my code", say "validate the Order entity in src/orders.riddl"
  2. Provide context: Share relevant parts of your model when asking questions
  3. Iterate: Use suggest-next to build models incrementally
  4. Learn from errors: Ask Claude to explain any validation errors you encounter

Back to MCP Overview

docs.title: Claude Desktop Configuration
docs.text: This guide explains how to configure Claude Desktop to use the RIDDL MCP Server for AI-assisted domain modeling.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Claude Desktop application installed
  • riddlg installed and on your PATH (see Installation): 
    brew install ossuminc/tap/riddlg

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Claude Desktop launches MCP servers as local processes (stdio transport) via a JSON configuration file.

docs.title: Configuration File Location
docs.text: Platform Path macOS ~/Library/Application Support/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json Windows %APPDATA%\Claude\claude_desktop_config.json Linux ~/.config/Claude/claude_desktop_config.json

docs.title: Adding the RIDDL MCP Server
docs.text:
Edit your configuration file to add the RIDDL server:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

That's the whole setup — no URL, no API key. Claude Desktop starts riddlg mcp for you when it launches.

docs.title: Complete Example
docs.text:
If you have other MCP servers configured, add RIDDL alongside them:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    },
    "filesystem": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "@modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem", "/path/to/files"]
    }
  }
}

riddlg must be found on PATH

Claude Desktop does not run your shell profile, so if riddlg isn't on the system PATH it may not be found. Use the absolute path (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/riddlg) as the command if the tools don't appear.

docs.title: Restart Claude Desktop
docs.text:
After modifying the configuration:

  1. Quit Claude Desktop completely
  2. Relaunch Claude Desktop
  3. The RIDDL tools should now be available

docs.title: Verify Connection
docs.text:
Ask Claude to validate some RIDDL:

"Can you validate this RIDDL code for me?"

docs.title: Gemini CLI Configuration
docs.text: This guide explains how to configure Google's Gemini CLI to use the RIDDL MCP Server for AI-assisted domain modeling.

docs.title: Prerequisites
docs.text:
• Gemini CLI installed (via Google)
  • riddlg installed and on your PATH (see Installation): 
    brew install ossuminc/tap/riddlg

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Gemini CLI uses a JSON settings file for MCP server configuration and can launch a local server over stdio.

docs.title: Configuration File Location
docs.text: Platform Path macOS ~/.gemini/settings.json Windows %USERPROFILE%\.gemini\settings.json Linux ~/.gemini/settings.json

docs.title: Adding the RIDDL MCP Server
docs.text:
Edit your settings file to add the RIDDL server under mcpServers:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

No URL and no API key — Gemini CLI runs riddlg mcp for you.

docs.title: Using the HTTP Transport Instead
docs.text:
If you prefer a long-running server (or want to share one), start riddlg serve and point Gemini at its HTTP endpoint:

riddlg serve            # listens on 127.0.0.1:8910

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "httpUrl": "http://127.0.0.1:8910/mcp"
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Verify Connection
docs.text:
Start Gemini CLI and test the connection:

gemini

Then ask:

Can you validate this RIDDL code? 

domain Example is { ??? }

Gemini should use the riddl_validate tool and return results.

docs.title: Tool Filtering
docs.text:
You can include or exclude specific RIDDL tools:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "includeTools": [
        "riddl_validate",
        "check-completeness",
        "explain-error"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Or exclude tools you don't need:

{
  "mcpServers": {
    "riddl": {
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"],
      "excludeTools": [
        "check-simulability"
      ]
    }
  }
}

Tool Precedence

If both includeTools and excludeTools are specified, excludeTools takes precedence.

docs.text:
Run Gemini CLI with verbose output:

gemini --debug

The debug output shows MCP server startup, tool discovery, and any error messages.

    riddlg validate "$file" || exit 1
done

docs.text: This guide explains how to configure VS Code with GitHub Copilot to use the RIDDL MCP Server for AI-assisted domain modeling.

docs.title: Prerequisites

• Visual Studio Code installed
  • GitHub Copilot and Copilot Chat extensions installed and activated

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: VS Code has built-in MCP support. Define the server once and Copilot's agent mode can use it. The simplest scope is per-workspace, in .vscode/mcp.json.

docs.title: Workspace Configuration
docs.text:
Create .vscode/mcp.json in your project root:

{
  "servers": {
    "riddl": {
      "type": "stdio",
      "command": "riddlg",
      "args": ["mcp"]
    }
  }
}

VS Code launches riddlg mcp as a local process — no URL and no API key. After saving, VS Code shows a Start action above the server entry; click it (or reload the window) to bring the tools online.

docs.title: User-Level Configuration
docs.text:
To make the server available in every workspace, add an mcp block to your user settings.json (open with Cmd+Shift+P → "Preferences: Open User Settings (JSON)"):

{
  "mcp": {
    "servers": {
      "riddl": {
        "type": "stdio",
        "command": "riddlg",
        "args": ["mcp"]
      }
    }
  }
}

riddlg must be found on PATH

If the tools don't appear, use the absolute path (e.g. /opt/homebrew/bin/riddlg) as the command.

docs.title: Verify Connection
docs.text:
1. Open Copilot Chat (Cmd+Shift+I or Ctrl+Shift+I) and switch to Agent mode
  2. Ask: "Can you validate this RIDDL code?" and paste some RIDDL
  3. Copilot should invoke the riddl_validate tool

You can see and toggle the available tools with the Tools picker in the Chat view.
